changes: Rename "line of good fit" to "line of best fit", the term the NSW Stage 5 syllabus uses.
Add a note that predictions beyond the range of the data are less reliable, since the card does not cover this caution.
match.reason: The bank card teaches the same idea of drawing a line by eye with points balanced either side, but it uses Victorian terminology and omits the required caution about predicting beyond the data.

confirm.reason: The Victorian 'line of good fit' card covers drawing by eye and reading off predictions, but it never teaches taking care when predicting beyond the data, which this brief requires. Adding that would be a new step rather than a small change, so a new point is safer.

draft.title: Lines of best fit
card: A line of best fit is a straight line drawn through a scatter plot to follow its trend. It is used when the correlation is clear.
Draw it by eye so that about as many points are above it as below it. It does not need to pass through any point.
To predict, read across from a value on the horizontal axis to the line, then to the vertical axis.
A prediction inside the range of the data is fairly reliable. A prediction beyond the data is much less reliable, as the trend may not continue.

2.alt: A scatter plot of eight points with a rising line of best fit through the middle. Four points lie above the line and four lie below it.

draft.remember: A line of best fit follows the trend. Trust predictions inside the data more than those beyond it.

a.q: Which describes a well-drawn line of best fit?
opts: It follows the trend, with points above and below
It passes through the first and last points
It passes through as many points as possible
It has all the points on one side of it
a.why: A line of best fit follows the trend and has about as many points above as below. Passing through the most points is tempting, but the line does not need to touch any point.
a.clue: Think about balance: points on both sides.

b.q: Mia plots the age of used cars (1 to 8 years) against their price and draws a line of best fit. Which prediction is most reliable?
opts: The price of a 5-year-old car
The price of a 12-year-old car
The price of a 15-year-old car
The price of a 20-year-old car
b.why: A car aged 5 years is inside the range of the data, 1 to 8 years. The other ages are beyond the data, so the trend may not continue there.
b.clue: Which age lies within the data Mia collected?
